How to read data using the cdasws Python package¶

reference:
https://pypi.org/project/cdasws/
https://berniegsfc.github.io/cdasws/jupyter/CdasWsDataRetrieval.html
https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/WebServices/REST/jupyter/CdasWsIdlExample.html

In [19]:
from datetime import datetime

from cdasws.cdasws import CdasWs, TimeInterval
from cdasws.datarepresentation import DataRepresentation as dr
from cdasws.doi import get_doi_landing_page_url, get_doi_badge_url, get_doi_hdp_url

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from IPython.core.display import HTML

today = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%B-%d')

def display_link(
    url: str,
    text: str) -> None:
    display(HTML(f'<a href="{url}" target="_blank">{text}</a>'))

def display_image_link(
    url: str,
    image_url: str) -> None:
    display(HTML(f'<a href="{url}" target="_blank"><img src={image_url}/></a>'))

Initialize the client¶

In [2]:
cdas = CdasWs()

List the dataset IDs¶

In [5]:
### user-specified ###
myobservatory=['ACE', 'Wind']
myinstrument =['Plasma and Solar Wind', 'Magnetic Fields (space)']
In [6]:
all_datasets = []
for obs in myobservatory:
    print('for %s' %(obs))
    datasets = cdas.get_datasets(observatoryGroup=obs,instrumentType=myinstrument)
    if datasets:
        all_datasets.extend(datasets)
        
    for index, dataset in enumerate(datasets):
        dataset_id = dataset["Id"]
        dataset_label = dataset["Label"]
        print(f'{index}. {dataset_id}, {dataset_label}')
        
    print('='*100)
    print(' ')

Show the URL/DOI of the selected dataset¶

In [8]:
mydois=[]
for index, dataset in enumerate(all_datasets):
    dataset_id = dataset["Id"]
    dataset_label = dataset["Label"]

    if dataset_id in mydataset:  # select this dataset for use below
        doi=dataset['Doi']
        #print(doi)
        mydois.append(dataset['Doi'])
        print(f'\nSelected dataset: {dataset_id} (doi:{doi})')
        print(f"Available Period: {dataset['TimeInterval']}")
        display_image_link(get_doi_landing_page_url(doi), get_doi_badge_url(doi))
        display_link(get_doi_hdp_url(doi), 'HDP Description')
        display_link(dataset['Notes'], 'CDAWeb Notes')
        display(HTML(f'<b>Data Citation</b>: {cdas.get_citation(doi)}.  Accessed on {today}.'))
        print('='*100)
        print(' ')

List the variables of the selected dataset¶

In [21]:
for indx,mydoi in enumerate(mydois):
    print('for %s' %(mydataset[indx]))
    variables = cdas.get_variables(mydoi)
    var_names = []
    for index, variable in enumerate(variables):
        name = variable['Name']
        var_names.append(name)
        print("'%s'" %(variable['Name']),"->", variable['LongDescription'])
    #    print(f'{index}. {name}, {variable["LongDescription"]}')
    print('='*100)
    print(' ')

for AC_H0_MFI
'Magnitude' -> B-field magnitude
'BGSEc' -> Magnetic Field Vector in GSE Cartesian coordinates (16 sec)
'BGSM' -> Magnetic field vector in GSM coordinates (16 sec)
'dBrms' -> RMS of Magnetic Field (16 sec period)
'SC_pos_GSE' -> ACE s/c position, 3 comp. in GSE coord.
'SC_pos_GSM' -> ACE s/c position, 3 comp. in GSM coord.
====================================================================================================
 
for AC_H0_SWE
'Np' -> Solar Wind Proton Number Density, scalar
'Vp' -> Solar Wind Bulk Speed
'Tpr' -> radial component of the proton temperature
'alpha_ratio' -> alpha to proton density ratio
'V_GSE' -> Solar Wind Velocity in GSE coord., 3 components
'V_RTN' -> Solar Wind Velocity in RTN coord., 3 components
'V_GSM' -> Solar Wind Velocity in GSM coord., 3 comp.
'SC_pos_GSE' -> ACE s/c position, 3 comp. in GSE coord.
'SC_pos_GSM' -> ACE s/c position, 3 comp. in GSM coord.
====================================================================================================
 
for WI_H0_MFI
'BF1' -> Magnetic field magnitude (1 min)
'BF1LOG' -> Magnetic field magnitude (1 min - log scaled)
'BRMSF1' -> RMS magnitude (1 min)
'BGSM' -> Magnetic field vector in GSM cartesian coordinates (1 min)
'BRMSGSM' -> RMS vector in GSM coordinates (1 min)
'BGSE' -> Magnetic field vector in GSE cartesian coordinates (1 min)
'BGSEa' -> Magnetic field vector in GSE angular coordinates (1 min)
'BRMSGSE' -> RMS vector in GSE coordinates (1 min)
'DIST' -> Distance from the center of the earth (Define Re = 6378km) (1 min)
'PGSM' -> Position vector in GSM coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 min)
'PGSE' -> Position vector in GSE coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 min)
'B3F1' -> Magnetic field magnitude (3 sec)
'B3F1LOG' -> Magnetic field magnitude (3 sec - log scaled)
'B3RMSF1' -> RMS magnitude (3 sec)
'B3GSM' -> Magnetic field vector in GSM cartesian coordinates (3 sec)
'B3RMSGSM' -> RMS vector in GSM coordinates (3 sec)
'B3GSE' -> Magnetic field vector in GSE cartesian coordinates (3 sec)
'B3GSEa' -> Magnetic field vector in GSE angular coordinates (3 sec)
'B3RMSGSE' -> RMS vector in GSE coordinates (3 sec)
'B1F1' -> Magnetic field magnitude (1 hour)
'B1F1LOG' -> Magnetic field magnitude (1 hour - log scaled)
'B1RMSF1' -> RMS magnitude (1 hour)
'B1GSM' -> Magnetic field vector in GSM cartesian coordinates (1 hour)
'B1RMSGSM' -> RMS vector in GSM coordinates (1 hour)
'B1GSE' -> Magnetic field vector in GSE cartesian coordinates (1 hour)
'B1GSEa' -> Magnetic field vector in GSE angular coordinates (1 hour)
'B1RMSGSE' -> RMS vector in GSE coordinates (1 hour)
'DIST1' -> Distance from the center of the earth (Define Re = 6378km) (1 hour)
'P1GSM' -> Position vector in GSM coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 hour)
'P1GSE' -> Position vector in GSE coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 hour)
'DISTV' -> Time axis label: Distance from the center of the earth (Define Re = 6378km) (1 min)
'PGSMV' -> Time axis label: Position vector in GSM coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 min)
'PGSEV' -> Time axis label: Position vector in GSE coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 min)
'DIST1V' -> Time axis label: Distance from the center of the earth (Define Re = 6378km) (1 hour)
'P1GSMV' -> Time axis label: Position vector in GSM coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 hour)
'P1GSEV' -> Time axis label: Position vector in GSE coordinates (Define Re = 6378km) (1 hour)

Download data¶

In [10]:
#show again the name of mydatasets for a reference 
print(mydataset)

['AC_H0_MFI', 'AC_H0_SWE', 'WI_H0_MFI']
In [11]:
# assign parameteprs
#dataset_id = 'AC_H0_SWE'
myvariables  = {}
mystart_time = {}
myend_time   = {}

### user-specified ###
myvariables[mydataset[0]]=['BGSM']
myvariables[mydataset[1]]=['Np', 'Vp','V_GSM']
myvariables[mydataset[2]]=['BGSM']
mystart_time[mydataset[0]] = '1998-02-04T00:00:00Z'
mystart_time[mydataset[1]] = '1998-02-04T00:00:00Z'
mystart_time[mydataset[2]] = '1998-02-04T00:00:00Z'
myend_time[mydataset[0]]   = '1999-02-04T00:00:00Z'
myend_time[mydataset[1]]   = '1999-02-04T00:00:00Z'
myend_time[mydataset[2]]   = '1999-02-04T00:00:00Z'
#######################


# request the data representation as Spacepy
data={}
for dataset in mydataset:
    print(dataset)
    status, data[dataset] = cdas.get_data(dataset, myvariables[dataset], mystart_time[dataset], myend_time[dataset], dataRepresentation = dr.XARRAY)
    if status['http']['status_code'] == 200:
        print('Donwload Success!')
    else:
        print(f"Error! HTTP Status Code: {status}")

    contour = ax.contourf(Theta, V, np.log10(dat_3d['ions_3d__C1_CP_CIS_CODIF_HS_H1_PEF'][it,indx,:,:]+1e-10), levels=100, cmap='jet')
    clear_output(wait=True)
    display(fig)

If you want to convert the SPCEPY-type data into a Panda dataframe¶

Here is optional. Please use the data with the Spacepy data type (Change to dataRepresentation=dr.SPACEPY in the data_get line above).

In [ ]:
df={}
for dataset in mydataset:
    print('for %s' %(dataset))
    cdf_copy=data[dataset].copy()
    data_dict = {key: cdf_copy[key][...] for key in cdf_copy.keys()}
    #print(data_dict)
    
    first_var_name=list(data[dataset].keys())[0]    #hope the first element is Epoch
    num_elements=len(data[dataset][first_var_name]) 
    
    # since Panda dataframes requires a flat data when converting, we need to flatten the data.
    flat_dict = {}
    flat_attrs = {}
    for key, value in data_dict.items():
        print(key,value.ndim,value.shape)
        # Check if the variable is 2D (e.g., Shape is [Time, 3])
        if value.ndim == 2: 
            if value.shape[1]==3: 
                labels = ['X', 'Y', 'Z'] # Fallback labels
                
                # Expand columns out individually
                for i in range(value.shape[1]):
                    flat_dict[f"{key}_{labels[i]}"] = value[:, i]
                
                    flat_attrs[f"{key}_{labels[i]}"]= data_dict[key].attrs
        else:
            if value.shape[0]==num_elements:
                flat_dict[key] = value
                flat_attrs[key]= data_dict[key].attrs
    
    df[dataset] = pd.DataFrame(flat_dict)
    df[dataset] = df[dataset].set_index(first_var_name)
    df[dataset].index.name='time'
    df[dataset]=df[dataset].mask(abs(df[dataset])>1e30)
    
    ### add attributes
    for key in df[dataset].keys():
        df[dataset][key].attrs=flat_attrs[key]
    
    print(df[dataset].head())
    print('='*100)
    print(' ')
